sample_unit: CT and MR radiology reports (full dataset; blinded radiologist ratings on a test subset)

links.outcome: Inter-radiologist agreement on impression quality ratings (ICC)
links.effect: Agreement among radiologists was low (ICC 0.22-0.49), indicating that expert-derived grading is inconsistent.

links.outcome: Correlation of automated NLP metrics with radiologist ratings
links.effect: Automated metrics showed weak correlation with human evaluation (ρ < 0.32); standard NLP metrics poorly reflect clinical relevance.
links.quote: Automated metrics showed weak correlation with human evaluation (ρ < 0.32).

unlisted_practices: Domain-adaptive pretraining of an LLM on radiology text versus fine-tuning only for report impression generation
Comparing open-source fine-tuned models with a commercial out-of-the-box model on harmful output rates

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates LLMs for generating radiology impressions using expert clinician evaluation, but primarily investigates model training/adaptation strategies (domain adaptation vs fine-tuning sample sizes) rather than a specific deployment guardrail or practice.
